intro.label: Overview
intro.heading: Bernedoodle vs Aussiedoodle: The Quick Answer
intro.html:
Both are popular Doodle hybrid breeds. The decisive practical differences: energy level (Aussiedoodle is significantly more energetic), temperament with kids (Bernedoodle is famously gentle; Aussiedoodle can be nippy due to herding instinct), size (Bernedoodle Standard is 20-30 lbs heavier), and signature look (Bernedoodle's tri-color vs Aussiedoodle's merle).

Last updated May 2026 - by Kailun Zhang

quick_answers.label: Quick Answers
quick_answers.heading: 5 Questions Most People Ask First
quick_answers.html:
Short answers to the questions most people ask before comparing these two:

Q: Which is calmer?

A: Bernedoodle, clearly. Bernese contributes calm temperament; Aussie contributes herding-breed energy.

Q: Which is smarter?

A: Aussiedoodle, slightly. Australian Shepherds rank in top 10 most intelligent; Bernese are moderately intelligent.

Q: Which is better with kids?

A: Bernedoodle, by a clear margin. Aussiedoodles can be nippy at running children (herding instinct).

Q: Which sheds less?

A: Both shed similarly when bred from F1B or multigen lines. F1 puppies can shed more.

Q: Which lives in an apartment better?

A: Bernedoodle Mini. Aussiedoodles need 60-120 min daily exercise plus mental work.

temperament.label: Personality
temperament.heading: Temperament: Gentle Giant vs Working Brain
temperament.html:
Bernedoodle: gentle, patient, calmer-paced

Bernedoodles inherit Bernese Mountain Dog's calm demeanor. Notably gentle with young children, less reactive to noise.

Aussiedoodle: smart, agile, herding-driven

Aussiedoodles inherit Australian Shepherd working drive and intelligence. They learn faster, excel at agility, but herd children (nipping at heels of running kids).

health.label: Health
health.heading: Health: Hybrid Vigor With Different Specific Risks
health.html:
Bernedoodle-specific

Cancer risk from Bernese side. Addison's disease from Poodle side. Sebaceous adenitis.

Aussiedoodle-specific

MDR1 mutation (drug sensitivity, DNA testable) - critical. Collie Eye Anomaly. Double-merle risk in puppies from poorly-bred litters.

mikes_take.label: Personal Take
mikes_take.heading: What I'd Tell a Friend Choosing Between These Two
mikes_take.html:
A first-time owner's take

If you're choosing between these two and have young children, get the Bernedoodle. Aussiedoodles are wonderful dogs for school-age kids who can play structured games and don't trigger herding instincts with random running and screaming. With toddlers, the Aussiedoodle's herding nips - even when 'just play' - become a real management challenge.

If you don't have kids and want a smart agility partner, Aussiedoodle wins. Match the dog to the actual household activity level, not the look you want.

mistakes.label: Common Mistakes
mistakes.heading: Mistake Index: Buyer Errors to Avoid
mistakes.html:
These are the most common buyer mistakes Wooffy sees come up repeatedly in owner forums and rescue intake stories. Knowing them ahead of time is the cheapest way to avoid 3-5 years of regret.

Mistakes new Bernedoodle owners often make

  • Buying F1 without understanding shedding lottery. F1 Bernedoodles inherit Bernese coat genetics ~50% of the time. F1B or multigen produce reliably low-shedding coats.
  • Not asking about cancer history from Bernese side. Bernese have one of the highest cancer rates of any breed. Ask for longevity history of Bernese grandparents.
  • Buying from non-ABDC affiliated breeder. The Bernedoodle Association of North America (ABDC) sets health-testing standards.
  • Underestimating Standard size at maturity. Standard Bernedoodles hit 80-90 lbs. Budget for giant-breed food and vet costs.
  • Not committing to professional grooming. Coats mat severely without professional grooming every 6-8 weeks.

Mistakes new Aussiedoodle owners often make

  • Buying from a merle-to-merle breeding. Double-merle puppies have severe deafness and blindness rates. Reputable breeders never breed two merles together.
  • Underestimating the energy requirement. Aussiedoodles need 60-120 min intense daily exercise plus mental work.
  • Apartment living without exercise commitment. Living in a 2-bedroom with one daily walk produces a neurotic dog.
  • Not asking about MDR1 testing. MDR1 mutation can make common veterinary drugs (ivermectin, loperamide) fatal. DNA test on both parents is essential.
  • Buying for 'smart dog' without committing to mental work. Smart dogs without jobs find their own jobs, usually destructive.

breeder_vetting.label: Breeder Vetting
breeder_vetting.heading: How to Vet a Breeder for Either Doodle
breeder_vetting.html:
Both breeds have committed reputable breeders and a wide pool of backyard breeders with no health testing. The questions below separate the two.

Ask any Bernedoodle breeder

  1. OFA hip and elbow certificates for both parents.
  2. OFA cardiac clearance on both parents.
  3. Longevity history of Bernese grandparents - past age 9?
  4. Are you a member of the Bernedoodle Association of North America (ABDC)?
  5. Which generation is the puppy (F1, F1B, F2, multigen)?

Ask any Aussiedoodle breeder

  1. OFA hip certificates for both parents.
  2. MDR1 DNA test results on both parents.
  3. Collie Eye Anomaly (CEA) DNA test on the Aussie parent.
  4. What are the coat colors of both parents? (No merle-to-merle breeding.)
  5. Do you start socialization, crate exposure at 4 weeks?

Red flags - walk away if you see any of these

  • Breeds merle-to-merle Aussiedoodles (lethal-white puppies).
  • Markets "rare merle" at premium prices.
  • Multiple Doodle varieties on offer simultaneously.
  • Will not share OFA database links.
  • Claims puppies are "hypoallergenic" without explaining F1 coat variability.
  • Sells puppies before 8 weeks old.

decision.label: Decision
decision.heading: Which Should You Choose?
decision.html:
Choose Bernedoodle if you...

Want a calmer Doodle. Have young children. Prefer tri-color look. Live in cool climate.

Choose Aussiedoodle if you...

Want smart, agile companion for active outdoor life. Have school-age children. Love merle look. Can commit to 60-120 min daily exercise + mental work.

faq.q: Which is better for first-time owners?
faq.a: Bernedoodle, slightly. Calmer temperament is more forgiving.
Single-merle Aussiedoodles are healthy. The risk is merle-to-merle breeding which produces ~25% double-merle puppies with deafness/blindness.

faq.q: Do Bernedoodles really live longer than Bernese?
faq.a: Yes, substantially. Hybrid vigor extends lifespan from Bernese's 7-10 years to Bernedoodle's 12-15 years (Standard) or 14-17 (Mini).

faq.q: What's the difference between F1, F1B, and multigen?
faq.a: F1 = 50% Poodle, variable coats. F1B = 75% Poodle, reliably low-shedding. Multigen = third-gen+, most consistent.

faq.q: What about Sheepadoodle or Goldendoodle instead?
faq.a: Both worth considering. See Sheepadoodle vs Bernedoodle and doodle comparison.
